did_you_know.text: Did you know? In Isaiah, Babylon is portrayed as a royal figure who has fallen from her position: she is commanded to come down from her throne and sit in the dust, no longer "tender and delicate" as she once was.
Did you know? Babylon’s humiliation includes a change from a life of luxury to hard labor: she is told to take a millstone, grind flour, and cross rivers, while exposing herself.
Did you know? The uncovering of Babylon’s nakedness represents the removal of her honor and protection; the prophet portrays her downfall as the exposure of her shame before everyone.

Did you know? In the prophecy of Babylon’s downfall, God is given the significant title: "Our Redeemer—the LORD of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel," emphasizing Israel’s redemption and God’s holiness.
Did you know? Babylon is commanded to sit in silence and darkness because she will no longer be called "the mistress of kingdoms." This highlights the loss of her ruling status.
Did you know? Although the LORD handed His people over to Babylon, the prophet holds her morally responsible: she showed them no mercy and placed an especially heavy burden on the elderly.

Did you know? Babylon also sinned through excessive self-confidence: she said in her heart that she would remain mistress forever, but she gave no thought to the future and did not consider that her position could change.

Did you know? Babylon is portrayed as a city living securely and saying, "I am, and there is no one besides me"; she imagines that she will never be a widow or know the loss of children, but this confidence proves to be complacency.
Did you know? The prophet declares that two calamities—loss of children and widowhood—will come upon Babylon "in a moment, on a single day," meaning suddenly and with great force.
Did you know? Isaiah mocks Babylon and challenges her to rely on her sorceries, wise men, and astrologers, but later makes clear that none of these can save her from disaster.
